newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria buys wheat from Canada, Syria -traders.
newsitem.headline: Algeria buys wheat from Canada, Syria -traders.

text.p: Algeria bought at least 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat from Syria and 100,000 tonnes of milling wheat from Canada, European grain traders said on Thursday.
There was no official confirmation of the deals and price details were lacking.
There was talk that Algeria may also have bought additional durum wheat tonnages from Canada.
"There is every reason to believe they also bought durum from Canada," one exporter said.
He said that Canada had been eager to sell its wheat, particularly its durum to Algeria in past months.

Last Friday Algeria tendered for the purchase of 75,000 tonnes of optional-origin soft wheat for September and 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat for August and September from Canada, the United States or Syria.
Traders said the general assumption was that Algeria bought the milling wheat in a closed deal with the Canadian Wheat Board (CWB) and decided to pass on the optional-origin tender.
Exporters said that because the Algerian government dealt directly with the CWB and with Syria details of the transactions would be very hard to obtain.
